object.definition: The environment fixes reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ supported on $[0,1]$, with means $\mu_{t,i}$ and variances $\sigma_{t,i}^2$. Rewards are independent across rounds and may be dependent across arms within a round. Public budgets Q,B satisfy $\sum_t\max_i\sigma_{t,i}^2\le Q$ and $\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty\le B$.

bindings.source_value: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.

The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
The native objective is $\inf_{\mathcal A(K,T,Q,B)}\sup_{(\nu_{t,i})\ \mathrm{obeying}\ Q,B}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\nu}[R_T]$.

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

objects.definition: The environment fixes reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ supported on $[0,1]$, with means $\mu_{t,i}$ and variances $\sigma_{t,i}^2$. Rewards are independent across rounds and may be dependent across arms within a round. Public budgets Q,B satisfy $\sum_t\max_i\sigma_{t,i}^2\le Q$ and $\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty\le B$.
mu_{t,i}=E_{nu_{t,i}}Y; the entire deterministic mean schedule is fixed before interaction.
The variance $\sigma_{t,i}^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{t,i}}Y$ is a deterministic property of the fixed environment.

protocols.adversary_information: Distributions or functions are fixed before interaction. A round’s fresh sample is drawn after the action and probes are chosen, independently of past history and the learner’s private randomness.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: The selected arm's mean gap; realized reward noise is excluded from the objective expression.
protocols.past_requery: The learner may not request new information from past rounds or previously used samples. Previously received feedback may be stored and processed. In stochastic models, an action may be repeated in a new round, using a fresh charged sample.
protocols.queries_per_round: T rounds give T bounded reward samples. Q and B are model assumptions, not additional free oracles.
steps: All reward marginals are fixed in advance. K, T, Q, and B are public.
Select $a_t$ using the history and private randomness.
A fresh reward from the current arm is returned; other arms' rewards are not revealed within that round.
